protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: bradford (well A1 in slot 5)
   line 80:  p300.aspirate(250, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 80 the tip went into bradford (well A1 in slot 5) while it still carried standard
   1 (well A6 in slot 3), standard 2 (well B6 in slot 3), standard 3 (well C6 in slot 3),
   standard 4 (well D6 in slot 3) and 23 more from an earlier step (this line did it 27
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   it then took the unwanted material along into 46 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   B2, B3, B4 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Also reached 46 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 80 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [0f4bc7936962]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 48 wells: 2 × 200 ul in 255 to 300 ul
   line 82:  p300.mix(2, 200, plate[well])
   At line 82 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 3 with
   2 strokes of 200 ul in a well holding 255 to 300 ul (this line did it 48 times). 2
   strokes of 200 ul move 1.33 to 1.57 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of
   strokes to mix (the mixing work). Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws
   over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What
   the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every
   later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (204 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 204,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [ebaac6d4e1f8]

3. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 80:  p300.aspirate(250, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 80 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 5 while it still carried
   standard 1 (well A6 in slot 3), standard 2 (well B6 in slot 3), standard 3 (well C6 in
   slot 3), standard 4 (well D6 in slot 3) and 23 more from an earlier step (this line did
   it 27 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid
   it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A
   reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every
   reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the
   next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well
   that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was
   later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 46 other
   wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Also reached 46 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 80, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [86e72e3928e9]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
